summary: High 5xx rate after customer webhook retry storm leading to apigw saturation and runtime OOMs
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported a sudden elevation in 5xx responses for a subset of streaming and short-poll routes after a large webhook delivery retry storm from their downstream service. The API gateway returned a mix of 502/503/504 and we observed multiple serving runtimes hit OOMs and restart loops.

Impact:
- Multiple production tenants saw increased 5xx rate and elevated latencies for 30+ minutes.
- Noteable Analytics (enterprise) experienced degraded availability for inference routes used by their ingestion pipeline.

Environment:
- Prod cluster: us-east (api-gateway fronted)
- Deployment: Hosted Redwood API (shared pool) with pinned model variant for customer routes

Steps to reproduce (reliable on load):
1) Customer resubmitted ~1200 webhooks within a 1-minute window (retry storm).
2) Each webhook triggers a short inference request and a streaming acknowledgement.
3) Apigw accept-queue and handshake concurrency spiked; hedged/async retries amplified load.
4) Serving runtimes started showing KV-prefetch timeouts followed by GPU memory growth and eventual OOM kills.

Observed behaviour / Logs / Metrics:
- Apigw metrics: accept_queue_depth rose from ~50 to >1200 in 40s; 5xx rate jumped from 0.2% to 8.6%.
- Runtime logs: repeated "OutOfMemoryError: GPU memory exceeded" from runtimes handling customer shard; then process restart.
- Autoscaler: delayed scale-up due to short-lived ephemeral worker churn.
- Traces: significant hedged-retry amplification on routes with 3xx/4xx observations.
- Customer supplied delivery logs: bulk resend timestamps and webhook headers attached in the ticket.

Links:
- Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ops/apigw-accept-queue?from=now-1h&to=now
- Runtime logs (sample): https://logs.redwood.internal/query?query=SUP-1184723

Immediate customer-facing workaround provided:
- Support recommended customer to disable aggressive webhook retries and enable exponential backoff (they confirmed temporary pause).
- We applied a temporary route-level concurrency cap and increased apigw accept-queue throttling for the affected route to prevent further runtime OOMs.

2026-03-12 10:26 - Customer (Noteable Analytics): Provided a CSV of retry timestamps; admitted a downstream worker bug caused concurrent resends.
2026-03-12 10:45 - SRE (Marco Reyes): Observed apigw accept_queue flood and multiple runtime OOMs. Temporarily capped route concurrency and notified customer to pause retries.
2026-03-12 11:05 - SRE (Marco Reyes): Applied route-level token bucket (50/s) and adjusted hedged retry policy to be less aggressive for that tenant. Monitoring for recovery.
2026-03-12 11:40 - Support (Lena Patel): Customer confirmed degraded traffic subsided after pause; some manual replays still pending that we advised to stage.
2026-03-13 09:10 - Eng (Priya Nair): Identified contributing autoscaler sensitivity to short-lived runtimes; opened follow-up engineering task INT-33021 to tune warmup thresholds.
investigation_notes: Observed acceptance queue and apigw threadpool saturation correlating with customer retry window.
Runtime stack traces indicate repeated allocations in attention cache path leading to GPU memory fragmentation over repeated short sessions.
Hedged retry configuration on the gateway amplified inflight requests for slow handshake routes, contributing to burst multiplication.
Autoscaler did not spin up stable capacity because runtime processes died quickly after OOMs (thrash loop).
No evidence of model bug; load pattern and retries were primary driver.
resolution_notes: Short-term: Applied per-route concurrency cap and temporarily relaxed hedged retries; instructed customer to pause aggressive webhook retries and re-ingest in controlled batches. Medium-term: Engineering to adjust autoscaler warmup/eviction thresholds and add guardrail to detect tenant-driven retry storms and automatically engage circuit-shed. Follow-ups: INT-33021 created for autoscaler tuning; RFC for apigw adaptive retry dampening planned. Customer follow-up call scheduled 2026-03-14 to review replay strategy.
